messages:
mike (support): FYI incoming from a customer (AcmeCorp) — their SIEM ingest is missing structured audit fields (user_id, action) and ~10% of exported events show KMS decryption errors on the Splunk side. timestamp window: 2026-03-14T02:10:00Z - 02:32:00Z. Anyone on call for audit-export?

thomas (acct-cs): Confirming — customer provided event id `evt_6b3f9a` and a splunk HEC batch sample. They see truncated `details` and a lot of `kms:InvalidCiphertext` in Splunk connector logs.

olivia (eng-security): Thanks. Two possibilities: (1) forwarder payload size cap/truncation before HEC, (2) KMS envelope metadata (key-tag) not preserved so Splunk forwarder can't map to right CMK. Can you paste the forwarder logs for that window?

jess (eng-infra): Pasting trimmed logs from exporter (sensitive fields redacted):
```
[2026-03-14T02:11:03Z] export-worker=exporter-7: sending batch size=48 bytes=512000 dest=hec://splunk-prd
[2026-03-14T02:11:03Z] export-worker=exporter-7: WARNING: payload-truncated=true truncated_bytes=112000 event_ids=[evt_6b3f9a,...]
[2026-03-14T02:11:04Z] kms-client: EncryptEvent failed: AccessDenied for key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:alias/exporter (missing tag:env)
```
Looks like exporter hit `MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES` (we cap at 512k) and also a KMS error for some events — the exporter tries to add `env:<customer>` tag to the KMS request and if missing the key policy denies.

olivia (eng-security): That matches. If exporter truncates, structured fields at the tail can drop (we send JSON array of events). For KMS: are we sure the key-tagging logic ran for that tenant? Recent change in kms-client added conditional tag on customer onboarding (RFC #332).

jess (eng-infra): Repro steps I ran locally:
1) generate ~60 events, total batch ~600KB
2) exporter built batch -> upstream HEC request trimmed to 512KB by our batching gate
3) truncated last 12 events lost `details.user_id` and `action` keys
4) for tenant without `customer` tag in KMS key metadata, `EncryptEvent` returns AccessDenied
Command snippet: `./exporter --batch-max-bytes=524288 --tenant acme-saas --send`

sophia (sre): For customer impact: short-term: re-run export for that 22-minute window with smaller batch-size to avoid truncation and regen encrypted blobs after ensuring KMS tags exist. Long-term: we should (a) fail the export early when batch > cap rather than silently truncating, and (b) validate KMS key tagging during tenant onboarding.

thomas (acct-cs): Customer asked for immediate mitigation — can we do a targeted replay for `acme-saas` for 2026-03-14T02:10 -> 02:32? They need the audit events re-ingested to Splunk within 24h.

mike (support): I've opened ticket #SUP-9873 and attached the customer's sample HEC payload and our logs. Taking action: run targeted replay + ensure KMS key tags are present before re-encrypt. Tagging @jess and @olivia to coordinate.

jess (eng-infra): Plan: temporary fix script `exporter-replay --tenant acme-saas --start 2026-03-14T02:10 --end 2026-03-14T02:32 --max-batch-bytes 200000` (will split batches client-side). Also adding a pre-send check to abort + log if any event exceeds single-event size or batch > cap. I'll run replay in staging review, then prod. ETA 45m.

olivia (eng-security): I'll validate KMS key metadata for acme-saas and add missing tags (requires IAM approval). If IAM blocks, we can temporarily use a fallback exporter key that has permissive policy (audit-only) but must document for compliance.

infra-bot: deploy/exporter-replay job queued (job id job-20260314-112).

sophia (sre): Post-action: we should add an alert when exporter returns `payload-truncated=true` and increment a per-tenant counter; that will catch this earlier. Also add a SIEM mapping test in our e2e that verifies `user_id`/`action` fields survive a roundtrip.

jess (eng-infra): Running replay now in prod with `--max-batch-bytes 200000`. Will post completion and Splunk ingestion confirmation.

mike (support): Thanks — keep me posted. I'll tell AcmeCorp we're doing a targeted replay and will confirm when Splunk shows the missing fields. :thumbsup:
